text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High p99 decode latency detected on dispatcher-prod for /v1/generate/stream (service: inference-stream). Thresholds: p95 > 200ms, p99 > 750ms. Current: p95=310ms, p99=1.2s, error-rate stable. Paging oncall.
samantha.chen: ack-ing, I'm oncall. seeing the same in the dashboard: spike started ~11:56 UTC. Customer impact: streaming stalls reported from a handful of PLG customers; CS pinged. @jake.wilson can you join? :phone:
jake.wilson: on it. linking trace: https://velocity/redwood/traces?trace=abcd1234 -- lots of long tail in decode stage (kernel call). Suspect new compile path / kernel change. Anyone who picked up the compile rollout? :thinking_face:
priya.rao: I rolled the compiler flags to enable FMHA microkernel optimizations in the runtime build earlier today at 09:15 UTC. Build tag: runtime-2026-03-14-fmha. This touched NVCC flags and toggled USE_FLASH_ATTENTION=true for trt backend.
luis.ortiz: running quick percentiles on prod trace logs. command:
```
curl -s "https://api.metrics/p99?service=inference-stream&since=12m" | jq '.p95,.p99'
```
output:
```
310
1200
```
confirming p99 ~1.2s. Also grep of agent logs shows repeated kernel timeouts in decode path:
```
[decode] kernel_call(ms)=1120 model=redwood-7b-q4 kernel=trt_fmha_v2 compile=runtime-2026-03-14-fmha
```
anna.khan: CS reporting 3 customers saw streaming stalls & reconnects. low volume but high severity for those apps. Keeping them updated.
samantha.chen: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching for streaming routes, 2) force fallback to legacy attention kernel for redwood-7b-q4, 3) revert compile flags if needed. Which is quickest?
jake.wilson: fastest is to flip runtime feature flag to fallback kernel. I can push a traffic rule to prefer legacy attention impl for that model. Doing now.
jake.wilson: `PATCH /config/routes` -> add rule: `if model==redwood-7b-q4 && route==/v1/generate/stream then kernel=legacy_fmha` — applying.
deploy-bot: deploy started: cfg-change-1779123580 by jake.wilson
luis.ortiz: monitoring... p99 dropped to 320ms within 40s after rule applied. p95 down to 260ms. Nice. But some pods still stuck with the newer kernel (old processes).
priya.rao: We can also hot-restart runtime workers on the affected ASG to pick up fallback rule faster. That will cause short 1-2s connection disruptions for a subset. Recommend rolling restart of 20% at a time.
samantha.chen: agree, do 20% rolling restarts. @jake.wilson coordinate.
jake.wilson: starting rolling restart group "inference-prod-asia-1" 20% at a time. command I'm running:
```
aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh --auto-scaling-group-name inference-prod-asia-1 --strategy Rolling --preferences '"MinHealthyPercentage":80'
```
luis.ortiz: logs after restart show p99 stabilized ~95-130ms for streaming decode on nodes using legacy kernel. But tail still spikes occasionally on a couple of hosts where the new kernel is still active.
priya.rao: I'm preparing an immediate revert of the compile flags (runtime-2026-03-14-fmha -> runtime-2026-03-13). That will require new build and deploy (longer). Should be a fallback if restarts + rule don't fully fix.
anna.khan: I've messaged the affected customers with a brief incident update and expected mitigation ETA ~10 min. They're okay with interim changes but want a postmortem.
samantha.chen: good. Next: check if this is regression from TRT/FlashAttention update. @priya.rao any recent TRT bump?
priya.rao: yes, the runtime build picked up TRT 8.8.3 and FlashAttention v2.1 at the same time as the FMHA switch. The compile path changed a couple of nvcc flags: `-lineinfo` enabled and `-O3` with `--use_fast_math`. I suspect a codegen path that interacts poorly with some GPUs for long sequences.
jake.wilson: we saw similar symptoms in staging when we enabled `USE_FLASH_ATTENTION` last month but didn't hit this tail. This time the compile flags + kernel selection created a path that's slower for long decode sequences (p99). Rolling back should fix.
luis.ortiz: alerting SRE that we should mark nodes with that kernel build and drain them for inspection after incident. `grep 'compile=runtime-2026-03-14-fmha' /var/log/runtime/*.log` finds ~12 hosts.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: cfg-change-1779123580 applied
samantha.chen: after rule + rolling restart, streaming p99 now ~110ms, p95 ~72ms. I'm marking incident mitigated. We'll hold on the compile revert for now but queue it as an emergency rollback if any reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:
priya.rao: starting a backfill build to produce runtime-2026-03-13 (no FMHA/FLASH) so we can revert quickly if needed. ETA ~30-45m for build + canary deploy.
jake.wilson: action items: 1) create postmortem runbook entry documenting kernel/compile-path regression, 2) add perf regression test that exercises long-streaming sequences on TRT+FlashAttention combo in CI, 3) label and drain hosts with runtime-2026-03-14-fmha. I'll create tickets.
anna.khan: CS will coordinate customer follow-ups and get exact impact windows to include in postmortem.
samantha.chen: handing off to night oncall @luis.ortiz for observation window. please escalate immediately if p99 > 400ms again or error-rate rises.
luis.ortiz: ack. I'll keep an eye for 4 hours, will post if anything flares. thanks all.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> partial rollback via config fallback + rolling restarts. Status: monitoring. SLA impact: transient p99 breach for ~18 minutes, minor customer reconnections for 3 tenants. Tags: kernel_regression, trt, flashattention, compile_flags, high_latency
samantha.chen: postmortem owners: jake.wilson (runtime), priya.rao (compile), luis.ortiz (sre), anna.khan (customer comms). Meeting to follow tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Closing thread for now.
